paragraphs: The blue finish on this generation of phone was produced in small numbers and became the one collectors remember. It is a reminder that a colour decision made for a single launch can outlive every specification on the box.

The model is very light at 10,107 polygons and 10,670 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 6 maps, 4 at 4096x4096 and 2 at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits product and technology visualisation, screen mockups, e-commerce imagery, period technology scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

The popcorn cart is Victorian street vending that never went away. The glass box, the red and gold trim and the wheels it will never actually roll on are all a costume, and the machine inside is entirely modern.
The model is light at 17,076 polygons and 17,637 vertices, built at subdivision level with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits event and venue visualisation, cinema and fairground scenes, retail and hospitality presentation, advertising, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2020.

The gyaling is a ceremonial instrument rather than a musical one in the western sense. It is played in pairs in Tibetan monastic ritual, in a continuous sound produced by circular breathing, and the tone is meant to carry rather than to please.
The model holds 132,920 polygons and 66,742 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in new condition. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits cultural and religious visualisation, museum and education work, musical instrument presentation, documentary graphics, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

Bergamot is grown almost entirely for its peel. The flesh is too sour to eat, the oil in the rind flavours tea and perfume, and the fruit exists commercially as a container for something on its surface.
The model is extremely light at 3,389 polygons and 3,369 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits food and beverage visualisation, packaging and menu imagery, cosmetics and fragrance presentation, advertising, kitchen scenes and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The security wand is deliberately simple. One control, one sound, and a search pattern the operator has been trained to follow in the same order every time, because the device provides no information about what it has found.
The model is very light at 12,024 polygons and 12,131 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $29 it suits security and event visualisation, equipment marketing, checkpoint and venue scenes, training material, film props and game environments. On sale since 2026.

The Hanukkah lamp has nine branches rather than seven, and the extra one is not counted among them: it is the servant flame used to light the others. That distinction is the whole structure of the object.
The model is extremely light at 4,454 polygons and 4,441 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in silver. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits religious and cultural visualisation, seasonal and interior scenes, decor and product imagery, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

The base of the Hearst building is a nineteen thirties facade with a glass tower grown out of it decades later. The original stonework and its figures were kept and hollowed out, which is preservation and demolition at the same time.
The model holds 54,287 polygons and 54,874 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits architectural and urban visualisation, heritage and facade presentation, city scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A flight case is furniture that expects to be thrown. Plywood, aluminium extrusion and recessed catches, built so that whatever is inside survives being loaded by somebody who is tired and running late.
The model holds 150,560 polygons and 77,766 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits event and touring visualisation, music equipment marketing, backstage and studio scenes, e-commerce imagery, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2023.

The top hat survived as formal wear long after it stopped being practical, and then survived again as a costume. It is one of very few garments recognised instantly by people who have never seen one worn seriously.

The model is extremely light at 1,711 polygons and 1,829 vertices, built in quads only with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 5 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits character wardrobe work, period and theatrical costume, game assets, advertising, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

Honey fungus is one of the largest living organisms on earth and a serious problem for trees. What appears above ground as a cluster of small mushrooms is the visible fraction of something spreading underground across acres.
The model is extremely light at 4,221 polygons and 4,223 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $29 it suits nature and forest visualisation, food and foraging imagery, education and documentary material, game environments, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.
The horseshoe shape comes from hanging. A sausage tied at both ends and hung over a rod to cure dries in that curve, and the form survived into modern production because customers now expect it.
The model is extremely light at 2,426 polygons and 2,422 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 3 maps up to 4096x4096. It carries StemCell certification.
At $29 it suits food and grocery visualisation, packaging and menu imagery, deli and market scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.
A fuel cell stack is a battery that never charges, because the fuel arrives from outside. The plates are stacked in series to reach a useful voltage, and the only exhaust from the reaction is water.
The model holds 47,980 polygons and 47,954 vertices, built in quads only with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits energy and technology visualisation, technical documentation, equipment marketing, education and research material, exploded views and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A pH probe is a battery whose voltage depends on acidity, which is a strange and elegant piece of chemistry. The glass bulb at the tip is the whole instrument, and it is fragile enough that most of the body exists to protect it.
The model is very light at 12,350 polygons and 12,491 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, shown immersed. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits laboratory and industrial visualisation, instrument marketing, technical documentation, education material, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A shoulder launched rocket in used condition tells a different story from a factory fresh one. Dust, scuffing and handling marks put the object in a supply chain rather than in a catalogue, which is what most scenes actually need.

The model is extremely light at 3,636 polygons and 3,742 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in dusty condition, textured with 5 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries StemCell certification.
At $29 it suits defence visualisation, documentary graphics, film and television props, game assets, simulation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.
